% Package watch (.github/workflows/nightly.yml): loads the packages the template patches, WITHOUT the
% template, and writes a fingerprint (MD5 of the definition) of every internal command it overrides, and
% whether every internal variable it uses still exists, to probe-fingerprints.txt. A changed line means a
% package update rewrote code the template patches: check that patch (the audit's patch inventory).
\DocumentMetadata{lang=en-GB, pdfversion=2.0, pdfstandard={ua-2,a-4f}, tagging=on,
  tagging-setup={math/setup={mathml-SE,mathml-AF}}, colorprofiles={X=FOGRA39L_coated.icc}}
\documentclass{book}
\usepackage{amsmath}
\usepackage[textsf]{ntxmath-otf}
\usepackage{graphicx,xcolor,tikz,longtable,url,cancel,listings,amsthm,makecell,hyperref}
\usepackage[chapter]{algorithm}
\usepackage{algpseudocode}
\usepackage[backend=biber]{biblatex}
% template/tagging.lua works with luamml's Lua code (not a public interface): fingerprints of the Lua
% functions it relies on, the callback it runs before, and the kernel's fake space it uses for listings
\directlua{
  probe = {}
  function probe.lua(file, name)
    local path = kpse.find_file(file, 'lua')
    if not path then return 'MISSING' end
    local f = io.open(path); local src = f:read('*a'); f:close()
    local nl = string.char(10)
    local s = src:find('function ' .. name .. '(', 1, true)
    if not s then return 'MISSING' end
    local e = src:find(nl .. 'end' .. nl, s + 1, true)
    return md5.sumhexa(src:sub(s, e or -1)):upper()
  end
  function probe.callback(cb, name)
    for _, d in ipairs(luatexbase.callback_descriptions(cb)) do
      if d == name then return 'exists' end
    end
    return 'MISSING'
  end
}
